name: MARJAPUSSI
description: Marjapussi is a four-player point-trick game from southern Finland. The name means 'bag of berries' but derives from the French 'mariage' (marriage of King and Queen), reflecting the game's unique mechanic where the trump suit is determined during play by declaring a marriage. Unlike its bidding variant Huutopussi, Marjapussi has no bidding - teams simply score based on points made in play.

content.text: Marjapussi is a four-player point-trick game from southern Finland. The name means 'bag of berries' but derives from the French 'mariage' (marriage of King and Queen), reflecting the game's unique mechanic where the trump suit is determined during play by declaring a marriage. Unlike its bidding variant Huutopussi, Marjapussi has no bidding - teams simply score based on points made in play.
A Finnish game whose name derives from French 'mariage' via the evolution: marias -> marjassi -> marjapussi. The 'bag of berries' meaning is a folk etymology.
4 players in two fixed partnerships, partners sitting opposite each other.
36-card pack: A, 10, K, Q, J, 9, 8, 7, 6 in each suit. Can use 32 cards (no 6s) or 28 cards (no 6s or 7s).
36-card pack: A, 10, K, Q, J, 9, 8, 7, 6 in each suit. Can use 32 cards (no 6s) or 28 cards (no 6s or 7s).

Deal and play clockwise. First dealer chosen at random. Dealer shuffles, player to right cuts. Deal all cards one at a time: 9 each with 36 cards, 8 each with 32 cards, or 7 each with 28 cards. Turn to deal passes left.

items.text: Tie carryover: If card points tie (no game point for majority), that point carries to next deal so taking majority next time scores 2 game points.
Ace of clubs leads: In the first deal, holder of ace of clubs leads to first trick and becomes second dealer; deal then rotates left as usual.
No beat requirement: Play without the requirement to beat the highest card in the trick; must still follow suit and trump when void. May be the original rule.
Lead ace first trick: Player who leads to first trick must lead an ace if possible; if no ace, must lead a spade if possible. Later tricks: any card may be led.
32-card pack: Use 32 cards (omit 6s); 8 cards each. Same rules otherwise. Requires deckType Standard 32 and rankSet Stripped_32.
28-card pack: Use 28 cards (omit 6s and 7s); 7 cards each. Same rules otherwise. Requires deckType Standard 28 and rankSet Stripped_28.
